validation_config.purpose: Configuration for scalar quantization (int8) benchmark validation #1344/#1717
validation_config.schema_prerequisite: Solr 10 ScalarQuantizedDenseVectorField uses supported bits (4 or 7) and Solr 9 staging rewrites bits 4/7 to vectorEncoding=BYTE

document_count.rationale: Large enough to stress memory (~750MB in float32, ~187MB in int8), small enough to complete in <10min per phase

benchmark_suite.excluded_reason: Keyword search is unaffected by vector quantization; focus on vector-dependent modes

modes.name: int8
modes.expected_memory_ratio_description: int8 should use ~25% of float32 memory (4x reduction)

release_blockers.description: Every semantic and hybrid query/mode comparison must have recall@10 ≥0.95 against float32, or be listed for explicit exception review before release claims
Query IDs, query file identity, search modes, top_k, collection, corpus ID, document count, and corpus bytes must match between float32 and int8 reports
Zero indexing or search errors during Phase 1 (float32) and Phase 2 (int8)
Attach same-host docker stats memory samples for every Solr node in both float32 and int8 runs; payload estimates alone are not acceptable evidence

warnings.description: int8 queries may be up to +10% slower; flag if >+15% (byte unpacking overhead)
Indexed document count must match between Phase 1 and Phase 2

phase_1.name: Float32 Baseline
steps: Capture memory: docker stats --no-stream solr solr2 solr3

phase_2.name: int8 Scalar Quantization Candidate
steps: Index SAME corpus (idempotent; indexer routes to embedding_byte_v)
Run SAME benchmark queries (order must match Phase 1)
validation: Query IDs and order match Phase 1

recall_at_k.description: Percentage of baseline top-10 documents found in candidate top-10

latency_delta_pct.description: Difference in query latency between int8 and float32

top_k_overlap.measurement: number of matching documents in top-k

required_files.name: benchmark-1344-float32.json
required_files.description: Full benchmark report with 60 results (30 queries × 2 modes)

required_files.name: benchmark-1344-int8.json
required_files.description: Full benchmark report with 60 results (int8 candidate)

required_files.name: benchmark-1344-quantization-comparison.json
required_files.description: Offline comparison with per-query recall@10 and latency delta

required_files.name: memory-1344-float32.txt
required_files.description: docker stats output for float32 baseline (MEM, LIMIT columns)

required_files.name: memory-1344-int8.txt
required_files.description: docker stats output for int8 candidate (should show 4x reduction)

readiness_status.current_state: PR #1670 has merged; Solr 10 scalar quantization schema now uses supported bits=7
readiness_status.current_schema_compatibility: Valid for Solr 10; Solr 9 staging rewrites supported scalar bits to DenseVectorField vectorEncoding=BYTE
readiness_status.schema_fix: bits="7" for Solr 10; Solr 9 compat rewrite to DenseVectorField vectorEncoding=BYTE
readiness_status.action_required: Execute paired float32 and int8 benchmark phases only in a controlled environment with the same representative corpus
readiness_status.remaining_blocker: Benchmark JSON, docker stats memory samples, corpus size, and failed query IDs are still required before publishing memory, latency, or recall conclusions

notes.idempotency: index_test_corpus.py deduplicates by Solr unique key; safe to re-run both phases
notes.offline_comparison: compare_quantization.py requires no Solr/Docker; suitable for CI pipelines
notes.sequential_execution: Each phase uses same Solr collection; must not overlap
notes.corpus_consistency: Phase 1 and Phase 2 must index the SAME corpus (same documents, same order) for valid comparison
notes.memory_measurement: docker stats captures live memory; run after indexing stabilizes (~1 min post-completion)
notes.query_order: Benchmark runner loads from queries.json in deterministic order; query_id must match between phases
